summary: Co-op resource-gathering minigame at Mos Le'Harmless where teams brew rum for pieces of eight and Honest Jimmy's cosmetic shop.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: 2+ player co-op resource-gathering and crafting minigame on the east side of Mos Le'Harmless (3813, 2973); games run 20 minutes with a 3-minute gap between them on the dedicated world (304).

facts.label: start
facts.value: Requires Cooking 40 (hard gate to access the minigame at all) and completion of the Cabin Fever quest; inventory, equipped head slot, and any followers must be empty to sign up.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Sign up with San Fan (blue team), Fancy Dan (red team), or Honest Jimmy (auto-balances to the smaller team); team members split into gathering roles (fetch water, dye it at colour stations, hunt sweetgrubs/bitternuts, chop scrapey bark) and processing roles (feed the boiler, keep its fire lit and pressure up, repair sabotaged/broken equipment, fend off a saboteur monkey) to fill hoppers that convert into rum bottles.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Payout is two-part: a flat 10 pieces of eight per rum bottle split across the whole team regardless of individual effort, plus up to 100 more pieces of eight scaled to a player's own contribution points (1 point per resource deposited, capped at 100; water buckets are the fastest point source, capping in about 3-4 minutes).

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Joining exactly at the 10-minute midpoint halves a player's pieces of eight but not their xp.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Crafting xp: 100 for contributing any non-water ingredient once per game, plus 12.5-50 per repair action. Cooking xp: 250 for contributing an ingredient once per game, plus 100-200 per ingredient added to a hopper. Firemaking xp: 150 for contributing an ingredient once per game, plus 50-100 per lit boiler log, doused fire, or sabotage.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Additional xp: Hunter for gathering sweetgrubs (40) and bitternuts (50), Fletching for scrapey tree bark (50), Agility and Hunter for capturing the saboteur monkey (15 each), and Strength for pumping boiler pressure (25).

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Honest Jimmy's shop, cleared at 39,590 total points, sells coloured naval shirts/tricorn hats/slacks in 7 colours, 6 pirate flags, 'the stuff' (boosts personal-brewing mature-ale odds), red/blue rum (consumable teleports back to the minigame), and a sellable medium clue scroll.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: A completed game (a win is not required) is a Morytania Diary Medium task.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The reward economy is entirely sunk into Honest Jimmy's cosmetic/QoL shop -- no combat and no skilling xp rate competitive with dedicated training; this is a social/cosmetic-farming minigame.

req_items.name: M'speak amulet
req_items.note: recommended but not required; unneeded once Monkey Madness II is completed

summary: Free-to-play safe-PvP capture-the-flag minigame between Saradomin and Zamorak castles, rewarding tickets for cosmetic gear.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Free-to-play (since 20 July 2017) safe-PvP capture-the-flag minigame, Saradomin vs Zamorak, 20-minute matches with 2+ players per side; entered west of Yanille (P2P entrance) or via the Ferox Enclave portal (F2P entrance) at (2407, 3105).

facts.label: start
facts.value: No skill, quest, or combat-level gate; only Castle Wars tickets, potions, runes, and combat armour/weapons may be brought in -- no food (bandages spawn inside instead), scarves, capes, or dwarf multicannon; alchemy, jewellery-enchant, and Lunar heal spells are disabled during a match.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Goal is to steal the enemy standard from the top floor of their 4-level castle and carry it back to your own castle's standard stand for a point; defenders can block with barricades, locked doors, and collapsible underground rock tunnels, or kill attackers outright.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Each castle has ground-floor gates (a breakable/barricadeable big door and a pickable/lockable small door), an outer-wall catapult, a team-only second-floor spawn room stocked with bandages, a third-floor trapdoor to that spawn room, a top flag floor, and an underground passage linking both castles' basements through a central cavern used for ranged/mage skirmishes.

facts.label: hazard
facts.value: Deaths inside the game are free -- no item loss, and players respawn inside the game.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: No xp is guaranteed by the minigame itself; ironmen specifically get zero combat xp inside Castle Wars, earning only splash Magic xp if casting with their own carried runes (not a rune pouch).

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Castle Wars tickets are earned per completed 15+ minute game, scaled by result and world type: a shut-out win pays 4, a regular win 3, a scoreless draw 2, and a drawn-with-points result 3 on dedicated Castle Wars worlds, one fewer each on non-CW worlds; both winner and loser earn some tickets.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: 1 plaudit is earned per ticket on dedicated Castle Wars worlds only, redeemable with Lanthus for a Castle Wars supply crate.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Lanthus's Ticket Exchange sells red/white/gold decorative armour sets (5-40+ tickets, usable in F2P), Saradomin/Zamorak hoods, cloaks, banners, and halos plus a Guthix halo (10-100 tickets, halos members-only), and decorative magic/ranged armour sets (members-only, 20-40 tickets each).

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: A full inventory blocks ticket pickup, and at least 15 minutes of participation is required to earn any tickets.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Entirely a PvP/cosmetics minigame -- no skill-training xp of note; the reward economy is pure decorative armour/capes/halos plus the plaudit resource-crate currency on dedicated worlds.

summary: 10v10 members PvP minigame on the Isle of Souls where Zeal Tokens buy combat xp and Nomad-shop cosmetics.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: 10v10 members-only team PvP minigame (Avatar of Destruction vs Avatar of Creation), 15-minute games, on the Isle of Souls, reached via the Soul Wars portal in the Edgeville/Ferox Enclave Dungeon (southwest of Edgeville bank) at (2206, 2900).

facts.label: start
facts.value: Requires 500 total level and 40 combat level, plus a one-time Nomad tutorial completion; no food, potions, capes, followers, or non-combat items are allowed into the tutorial, and the player must not be poisoned, envenomed, or diseased to enter it.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: The regular lobby auto-balances combat level across teams and needs 10+ players per side to start (20 players in the lobby starts the game in 4 minutes, scaling down to instant at 120); a separate east lobby handles clan-challenge games capped at 30 zeal.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Objective is to reduce the enemy Avatar's 100% starting damage reduction to 0% by controlling the Soul Obelisk, sacrificing soul fragments dropped by wandering monsters there (worth only 1/3 contribution if the enemy team controls it), while defending your own Avatar by burying bones at graveyards to raise its damage reduction (same 1/3 penalty if the enemy holds that graveyard).

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Team capes are locked on and make enemies the default left-click attack target; friendly fire is blocked entirely, and the minigame is PvP-enabled on PvP worlds just like the main game.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Zeal Tokens, the only reward currency, require staying on an activity bar that drains after about 3 minutes idle; letting it fully deplete ejects the player from the game with a 10-minute rejoin cooldown.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Zeal is earned by killing enemy players (scaled by relative combat level, diminishing on repeat kills of the same target), healing teammates, burying bones, sacrificing fragments, damaging the enemy Avatar, and capturing graveyards or the obelisk; NPC kills and barricade destruction earn zeal-bar activity credit but not zeal itself.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Losers earn up to 40 zeal, winners up to 60, and draws up to 50, so losing is not a wasted game.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Any combat skill at level 30+ can be trained by redeeming Zeal Tokens directly through Nomad, choosing skill and amount.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Zeal Token rewards from Nomad: Soul cape (2500 zeal, untradeable cosmetic/imbuable cape), Ectoplasmator (250 zeal, upgrades Ava's device/max cape for ammo-saving), Spoils of war caskets (30 zeal each), and Blighted supply sacks (entangle/teleport/vengeance/ancient ice runes, manta ray, anglerfish, karambwan, or super restore(4), all 10 zeal each, usable only within Wilderness/blighted-restricted content).

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: All Nomad rewards are gated purely behind Zeal Tokens; Soul Wars grants no other progression unlocks.

summary: Battle-royale PvP minigame with randomized max-gear loadouts, rewarding reward-shop points or High Stakes coin prizes.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Battle-royale PvP minigame, 4-24 players, started via Lisa at Ferox Enclave (3142, 3636); matches instance onto either a Desert Island or Wild Varrock map.

facts.label: start
facts.value: No skill, quest, or item requirement to enter Casual mode (4+ players, no payout); Competitive mode needs 24 players on members worlds and requires 750 total level plus 30 quest points (or 1500 total level with fewer quest points); High Stakes needs the same gate plus a 500,000gp buy-in, is disabled for ironmen, and is toggled on/off at Jagex's discretion.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Real inventory and equipment are confiscated for the match; every participant is handed one of three randomized max-gear loadouts (Max/Med 99/99/85/99/99/99, Zerker 80/99/50/99/99/99, or 1 Def Pure 75/99/1/99/99/99 across Attack/Strength/Defence/Magic/Range/Hitpoints) with a full Ancient Magicks/Lunar/Standard spellbook choice at a supply chest, with no quest or level prerequisites to cast any of it in-game.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Killing players fully heals and refills your own supplies and earns a bloody key (a bloodier key if fewer than 6 players remain) for a loot chest roll on offensive or defensive tables.

facts.label: hazard
facts.value: A shrinking safe-zone fog mechanic forces engagements: light fog begins after 1 minute, greater fog after 2:30 deals up to 10 damage per 2 ticks outside 16 tiles of the zone, and damage escalates rapidly after 10 minutes for anyone still outside it.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Forfeiting (logging out or taking the Desert Island rowboat) forfeits all reward; 3 forfeits in one day bans the player from Competitive and High Stakes for the rest of that day.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: LMS grants no skill xp at all, despite being F2P-accessible and handing out members-only gear/spells for the game's duration only -- this is the only place F2P accounts get to use members' weapons, special attacks, and Ancient Magicks.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Competitive mode performance points: 6 for 1st, 5 for 2nd, 4 for 3rd/4th, 3 for 5th-9th, 1 for 10th-19th, plus a non-stacking bonus of +2 for 3 kills or +3 for 5 kills; points are spent at Justine's reward shop, and tradeable rewards require having won at least 1 game.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: High Stakes mode: the winner takes 7,500,000 coins and the runner-up 2,500,000 coins, claimable anytime from a chest near Justine; 3rd-5th place get their next High Stakes entry fee waived.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: A pure PvP-skill/gear-simulator minigame with a coin-sink High Stakes economy -- no skilling relevance to a progression route beyond its own reward-shop cosmetics and gp.

summary: Solo instanced Farming minigame in Hosidius where depositing fruit earns Farming xp and points for Farmer Gricoller's shop.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Solo instanced Farming minigame in Hosidius, Great Kourend (1819, 3500).

facts.label: start
facts.value: Requires Farming 34 minimum to enter (boostable, but the boost must be active both when taking seeds and when planting them; watering and harvesting don't need it); 54 Farming is needed for Bologano seeds and 74 for Logavano seeds, though all tiers give identical points and gameplay, just different xp per plant.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: One seed tier (Golovanova/Bologano/Logavano) is chosen at the entrance and used for the whole session, up to 10,000 seeds; each planted patch must be watered 3 times before the 1, 2, and 3-minute marks or it wilts and dies, but a plant fully grown at 3 minutes can no longer die.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Gricoller's fertiliser, auto-given on entry, doubles growth rate but is generally considered less point/xp-efficient than the standard watering cycle.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Leaving through the door fully resets the instance (score and xp are kept, but inventory seeds/fruit are cleared); logging out mid-session keeps points and inventory but loses any crop still in the ground.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Farming xp is deposit-based and scaled by seed tier, with a 250x-harvest-rate bonus on the 75th fruit deposited (1500/3500/5750 xp for Golovanova/Bologano/Logavano) and double xp on fruits 75-100 of each 100-fruit batch.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Farmer Gricoller's Rewards shop is spent from points earned by depositing fruit (1 point per 3 fruit, plus a 2-point bonus per 100-fruit sack fill, capped at 16,000 held points): full farmer's outfit (400 points total across strawhat, jacket-or-shirt, boro trousers, boots), compost, supercompost, grape seeds, Bologa's blessings, herb box, seed pack, seed box, herb sack (needs Herblore 58), Gricoller's can, and an Auto-weed toggle; 1150 points clears the entire shop.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: A well-run 25-patch, 4-cycle-per-hour session earns roughly 35 points per 100-fruit harvest in about 19 minutes, meaning the full 1150-point shop takes roughly 10.5 hours of consistent play.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: No combat and no risk -- a purely repetitive plant/water/harvest/deposit loop, best framed as a single long uninterrupted Farming-xp-and-outfit grind rather than something interleaved in short bursts.

req_items.name: Watering can
req_items.note: recommended; or one Gricoller's can (a 1000-dose reward-shop upgrade) once points are available

summary: Solo gnome food/cocktail delivery minigame at the Grand Tree paying coin tips and rare item tips for completed deliveries.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Solo delivery-running minigame themed as gnome food delivery, started via Gianne jnr on the 1st floor of the Grand Tree (2437, 3500).

facts.label: start
facts.value: Requires Cooking 29 to complete the mandatory one-time tutorial (gnome-cooking with Aluft Gianne snr, gnome-cocktails with Blurberry); The Grand Tree quest is not hard-gated but strongly assumed by most delivery destinations and NPCs, and Monkey Madness II is recommended for the royal seed pod fast-travel back to the Grand Tree.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: The one-time tutorial teaches 4 gnome dishes (ingredients bought from Hudo) and 4 gnome cocktails (ingredients from Heckel Funch); afterward Gianne jnr hands out repeatable delivery jobs, either easy (in/around the Grand Tree, 6-minute limit, 1 point) or hard (anywhere in Gielinor including aggressive-NPC and desert-heat zones, 11-minute limit, 3 points).

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: The specific gnome food or cocktail ordered must be player-made -- premade restaurant/bar versions are rejected, though player-made items bought from the Grand Exchange are accepted; pre-stocking a bank tab of common orders is a standard efficiency trick.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Declining a hard delivery costs a 5:30 waiting penalty unless that time is spent on an easy job instead; tip value is independent of delivery speed.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Easy deliveries pay a flat 2-500gp coin tip regardless of delivery speed, as long as the time limit is met. Hard-delivery tips include gnome goggles/scarf (~23/384 each), gnomeball (10/128), 5 grand seed pods (23/512), mint cake (23/512), plus herbs, uncut gems, rare runes, mithril/adamant/runite bolts, bird nest, raw oomlie, pure essence, snake charm, half-keys, gold ore, and coal.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: A reward token system banks 1 point per easy delivery and 3 per hard delivery; every 12 points banks a free random gnome food item on the token (up to 10 items/120 points stored) as a pure QoL/food-farming mechanic, not a permanent unlock.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Once 10 unused reward tokens are banked, Gianne tells the player to go on vacation, letting them freely re-roll delivery targets by re-opening dialogue without completing the job and never triggering the 5:30 penalty -- this lets a player cherry-pick only the hard-delivery targets tied to rarer unique tips instead of grinding random jobs.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: A completed delivery is a Western Provinces Diary Medium requirement.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: No inherent xp gain from play itself beyond the one-time tutorial's Cooking xp -- value is purely in the tip-table loot and the food-reward-token QoL system, making this an intermittent side-loop for gnome goggles/scarf/grand seed pods rather than a skilling method.

summary: Solo trap-navigation maze under Burthorpe that drains Agility/Thieving for xp and rewards a rogue-outfit piece on a cracked safe.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Solo trap-navigation maze under Burthorpe, entered via a trapdoor near the bartender inside the Toad and Chicken inn (2906, 3537).

facts.label: start
facts.value: No entry requirement to walk into the Den itself (its shops, bank, and wall safes for uncut-gem cracking outside the maze are open at any level), but the maze proper requires unboostable 50 Agility and 50 Thieving; higher Agility/Thieving beyond that increase the trap-drain buffer and thus the effective safe-crack success rate. A player must enter with an empty inventory, no equipment, and no follower; a mystic jewel to leave at will is auto-granted on entry.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Route: run a fixed sequence past floor traps, pendulums, spinning blades, and wall traps using stand-then-run timing tricks (an 80-Thieving shortcut skips a long mid-maze detour), disable specific wall traps via right-click Search-wall, use flash powder on a guard near the end to stun and pass, then crack one of the exit wall safes to both claim a reward and teleport out.

facts.label: hazard
facts.value: Safe-crack success is a hidden roll against the player's current (drained) Thieving stat; failing has a 50% chance of ejection with no reward and a 50% chance of a further 1-point Thieving drain followed by a re-roll, so repeated attempts without resting Thieving compound the risk.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: A successful safe crack splits 3/8 into a rogue kit and 5/8 into an equipment crate; the rogue kit is a one-time convertible into a rope, chisel, tinderbox, or spade, while the equipment crate lets the player pick one piece (rogue mask +5 all defensive, top +10, trousers +7, gloves +2, boots +2) and can alternatively be redeemed as a kit instead.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Agility and Thieving each grant 12 xp per stat level drained while navigating traps; this can be farmed by intentionally jumping back and forth at the final pendulum to drain Agility down near 0-5 before cracking the safe, up to roughly 22,000 Agility xp/hour at 99 Agility/80 Thieving per the source page's own rate.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: The full rogue outfit gives a 15% chance per piece worn (guaranteed at a full set) to double pickpocket loot from any NPC; loot quantity only, xp is unaffected.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Martin Thwait's Lost and Found shop (50 Thieving + 50 Agility, or 99 Thieving alone) buys items at High Alch price rather than Low Alch and sells the Thieving cape/hood at 99 Thieving.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: The full rogue outfit is storable in a player-owned house costume room armour case once owned.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Expected time to a full rogue outfit set ranges from roughly 48 minutes at 50 Thieving down to roughly 22 minutes at 99 Thieving.

req_items.name: Energy potion
req_items.note: recommended but optional, for repeat maze runs

req_items.name: Stamina potion
req_items.note: recommended but optional, for repeat maze runs

summary: Solo Agility minigame beneath Brimhaven where tagging the active ticket dispenser earns Agility xp and Pirate Jackie the Fruit vouchers.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Solo Agility minigame on an underground course beneath Brimhaven (2809, 3194), structurally different from lap-based courses: 25 pillars linked by agility obstacles, 24 of which hold a ticket dispenser, with exactly one dispenser 'active' at a time on a rotating 1-minute timer.

facts.label: start
facts.value: No Agility level is required to enter (any level can attempt some obstacles); 20 Agility is needed to pass the pressure-pad/floor-spike obstacles and 40 to pass spinning blades and darts, with higher Agility reaching more of the course's dispensers. A 200-coin entry fee is paid to Cap'n Izzy No-Beard before each session.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: The player's task is to navigate obstacles to reach whichever dispenser just activated and tag it before it deactivates, earning direct Agility xp scaled to current Agility level (boosts included) plus a ticket and voucher pair banked for later exchange.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Best xp/hour comes from continuously running obstacles during the dead time between dispenser activations rather than standing idle waiting.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Tagging an active dispenser awards 30 xp per 10 Agility levels (including boosts/drains), capping at 300 xp if boosted to level 100; each Agility arena ticket separately converts to a flat, level-independent 345 Agility xp when redeemed with Pirate Jackie the Fruit (379.5 xp with Karamja gloves 2/3/4 -- the +10% applies only to this ticket-exchange xp, not the per-tag or obstacle xp).

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Each successfully-tagged active dispenser drops an Agility arena ticket and a Brimhaven voucher (10% chance of a double drop with the Karamja Diary Elite completed).

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Pirate Jackie the Fruit's voucher shop sells toadflax (3), snapdragon (10), a full graceful-outfit recolour (250, uncoloured pieces only -- won't recognise an already-upgraded graceful outfit), a pirate's hook (800), and amylase packs (60).

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: No combat xp or gear rewards -- purely an Agility-xp and cosmetic/herb sink.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Fastest known access is the Achievement Diary cape teleport directly to Pirate Jackie the Fruit; a player-owned house in Brimhaven with teleport-to-house is the next-best option if available.

summary: Ranged ammo-recovery backpack unlocked via Animal Magnetism, with three tiers gated by Ranged level.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Obtained from the NPC Ava after completing the Animal Magnetism quest; no additional gp cost beyond the quest.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Worn backpack that auto-recovers a percentage of fired Ranged ammunition (arrows, bolts, darts, javelins, throwing knives, axes, toktz-xil-ul) on each kill; recovery scales by tier: attractor (30 Ranged) lowest, accumulator (50 Ranged) mid, assembler (70 Ranged plus Vorkath's head) highest.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Also usable in Castle Wars (upgraded on Lanthus) and Soul Wars (upgraded on Nomad) to recover ammo in those minigames.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Does not recover ammo consumed on use (chinchompas, holy water) or weapon charges (blowpipe scales, webweaver ether) -- a passive cost-reduction accelerant for arrow/bolt/dart-based Ranged training rather than a blocking dependency.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The assembler tier is gated behind a second quest, Dragon Slayer II, for its Vorkath's head component; a fresh account may reach 70 Ranged well before finishing Dragon Slayer II.

summary: Staff crafted from a Dramen branch after Lost City that enables Zanaris entry and fairy-ring transport.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Crafted at Crafting 31 by using a knife on a Dramen branch cut from a Dramen tree on Entrana, after completing the Lost City quest.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Enables entry to Zanaris via the Lumbridge Swamp shed and activates the fairy-ring transport network; required in-hand to use any fairy ring until the player has also completed the Elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary, after which fairy rings work staff-free.

facts.value: Also usable during the Fremennik Trials to defeat Koschei the Deathless by smuggling in a branch and knife.

facts.value: Functionally superseded (better stats, autocast) by the lunar staff upgrade obtained from the Lunar Diplomacy quest.

facts.value: Cheap to duplicate, since Entrana access and the Dramen tree are both freely available after the Lost City quest -- crafting a spare immediately is a safeguard against loss.

summary: Slayer-reward headgear that combines six face/head items' effects into one slot, craftable at Crafting 55.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Crafted at Crafting 55 (boostable) by combining a nose peg, facemask, earmuffs, spiny helmet, enchanted gem, and black mask; requires Defence 10 to equip.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Combines the special effects of all six Slayer-reward face/head items it's crafted from (nose peg smell immunity, facemask, earmuffs, spiny helmet, enchanted gem, and the black mask's 16.67% Attack/Strength boost versus assigned Slayer tasks), plus rune-full-helm-equivalent defensive stats.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Doubles as warm clothing for Wintertodt and blocks Nex's infection virus attack.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Can later be imbued (via Soul Wars, Nightmare Zone, or Emir's Arena) to add a 15% Ranged and Magic accuracy and damage boost on task, stacking the whole kit into one equipment slot.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: A gear-consolidation unlock, not a blocking one -- the underlying six items must already be owned, each with its own Slayer-point, quest, or drop gate; the helmet merges their perks into a single slot plus grants the task-only combat boost the black mask alone doesn't confer outside Slayer assignments.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Reinforced goggles (requiring the A Porcine of Interest quest) are only needed as one of the six component items and are not otherwise a hard gate on the base helmet.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The helmet's Attack/Strength bonus does not stack with Salve amulet variants against undead tasks -- a route should not recommend using both at once.

summary: Enchanted emerald ring giving 8 charges of teleport to Emir's Arena, Castle Wars, Ferox Enclave, and the Fortis Colosseum.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Made by casting Lvl-2 Enchant on an emerald ring; the spell itself has a low Magic level requirement and no quest gate.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Provides 8 charges of teleport to Emir's Arena (Duel Arena), Castle Wars, and Ferox Enclave, crumbling to dust on the 8th use; a 4th destination, the Fortis Colosseum, unlocks after reaching Hero rank (12,000 glory) at the Colosseum.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: The Ferox Enclave teleport additionally grants a free full heal, prayer restore, and run-energy restore via the Pool of Refreshment on arrival.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The cheapest of the enchanted-ring travel items, needing no quest to make or use; primarily valued for the Ferox Enclave stop's free restore and proximity to Wilderness boss/skilling routes.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The Fortis Colosseum destination is a later unlock gated behind Colosseum glory rank, not available from a freshly made ring.

summary: Enchanted sapphire necklace giving 8 charges of teleport to Burthorpe, Barbarian Outpost, Corporeal Beast, Tears of Guthix, and Wintertodt Camp.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Made by casting Lvl-1 Enchant on a sapphire necklace; a very low Magic level with no quest gate.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Provides 8 charges of teleport to Burthorpe, Barbarian Outpost, Corporeal Beast, Tears of Guthix, and the Wintertodt Camp, crumbling to dust on the 8th use.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: On the last charge it's recommended to alch the necklace instead of using the final teleport, since alch value is charge-independent.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The cheapest enchant-tier travel jewellery alongside the ring of dueling; its destination spread is training/boss-access oriented rather than general travel, so its value is highly dependent on which of Wintertodt, Corporeal Beast, or the other listed activities the account is actually doing.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Tears of Guthix requires its own quest-count gate to be worth visiting.

summary: Enchanted dragonstone amulet giving rechargeable teleports to Edgeville, Karamja, Draynor Village, and Al Kharid plus combat bonuses.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Made by casting Lvl-5 Enchant on a dragonstone amulet; the amulet can be made and worn immediately for its combat bonuses with no quest requirement, but can only be recharged after completing Heroes' Quest.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Provides 4 charges of teleport (6 if recharged at the Fountain of Rune) to Edgeville, Karamja, Draynor Village, and Al Kharid, plus flat melee/ranged/magic damage-style combat bonuses while worn; rechargeable indefinitely once the quest gate is met.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Its dragonstone teleports still function up to level 30 Wilderness, unlike most teleports which cut off at level 20.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Recharging requires Heroes' Quest, a mid-length quest with its own prerequisite chain (Shield of Arrav, Lost City, Merlin's Crystal, Dragon Slayer I); a fresh account effectively cannot sustain glory-teleport use until that chain is cleared. Dragon Slayer II additionally unlocks recharging at the Fountain of Uhld.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Popular for its combined Al Kharid/Draynor/Karamja/Edgeville destination spread (banking, GE-adjacent, minigame, and desert-quest travel in one item) and its up-to-30-Wilderness range, making it a strong candidate for an early steer point once Heroes' Quest is in reach.

summary: Enchanted dragonstone necklace giving rechargeable teleports to the six gathering-skill training guilds.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Made by casting Lvl-5 Enchant on a dragonstone necklace; base recharging (at the Legends' Guild totem pole, the Fountain of Uhld, or via the Recharge Dragonstone spell) needs no quest at all.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Provides 4 charges of teleport (6 at the Fountain of Rune after Legends' Quest) to the Fishing, Mining, Crafting, Cooking, Woodcutting, and Farming Guilds -- a dedicated gathering-skill training hub network.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Shares the up-to-30-Wilderness teleport range of other dragonstone jewellery and gives a small (+0.4 percentage point) casket bonus while worn/charged during big-net fishing.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Legends' Quest only adds 2 extra charges via the Fountain of Rune, making this a lighter-gated travel item than the amulet of glory despite sharing the same dragonstone-jewellery mechanic.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Its destination set is narrowly gathering-skill-guild-focused (no combat or quest-hub stops), making it a niche accelerant specifically for guild-gated training routes rather than a general-purpose hub.

summary: Digsite pendant is a 5-charge teleport necklace near the Digsite, made by casting an enchant spell learned via The Dig Site and a rare museum-cleaning drop.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: 5-charge, non-rechargeable teleport necklace to north of the Digsite, made by casting the pendant's own enchant spell on a ruby necklace.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: The Dig Site quest is required to access the Varrock Museum specimen-cleaning process that teaches the enchant spell; it does not guarantee the clean-necklace roll on any fixed timetable.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Casting the enchant spell needs Magic 49, or can be substituted with an enchant ruby or topaz tablet.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Two more permanent destinations toggle on/off per pendant when used on strange machines: House on the Hill on Fossil Island (needs Bone Voyage) and Lithkren near the rune dragons (needs Dragon Slayer II).

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: A mounted version giving unlimited teleports to the same destinations needs 82 Construction and a curator's medallion placed in a POH portal nexus.

summary: Explorer's ring (tiers 1-4) is awarded by Hatius Cosaintus for each Lumbridge & Draynor Diary tier; the elite ring grants 30 free daily alchemy casts.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Tiered ring (1-4) awarded by Hatius Cosaintus in Lumbridge for completing the matching Lumbridge & Draynor Diary tier; free to re-obtain if lost.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The gate is Lumbridge & Draynor Diary tier completion rather than a craftable-item recipe; no separate quest or item requirement applies to the ring itself.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Elite tier (ring 4) grants 30 free casts/day of Low or High Level Alchemy with no runes or Magic xp cost, plus 3 free full run-energy restores/day and unlimited teleports to the Falador farm cabbage patch.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: A 2025 QoL update lets items be alched directly by using them on the elite ring instead of casting the spell manually.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Lower diary tiers grant a subset of the elite tier's perks plus other always-on diary-tier perks.

summary: Camulet is a 4-charge teleport necklace to Enakhra's Temple, rewarded from Enakhra's Lament and rechargeable with Ugthanki dung and a bucket.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: 4-charge teleport necklace to Enakhra's Temple in the desert near Lazim, awarded on completing Enakhra's Lament; free to reclaim from Lazim if lost.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Recharges with Ugthanki dung (from certain camels after partial completion of My Arm's Big Adventure) plus a bucket; an optional 1,000,000 coin payment to Lazim upgrades it to unlimited charges.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Switches to teleport near the Bandit Camp Quarry entrance instead, once the Hard Desert Diary is complete.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: Using the camulet to reach Enakhra's Temple is itself a requirement of the Medium Desert Diary.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Also lets the wearer speak to certain camels (e.g. Al the Camel in Al Kharid) found across the Kharidian desert.

req_items.note: obtained from certain camels after partial completion of My Arm's Big Adventure; used with a bucket to recharge the camulet

req_items.note: used with Ugthanki dung to recharge the camulet

summary: Ectophial is an unlimited-use quest reward from Ghosts Ahoy that teleports to the Ectofuntus outside Port Phasmatys, auto-refilling after each use.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: One-click, unlimited-use teleport to the Ectofuntus outside Port Phasmatys, awarded on completing Ghosts Ahoy with no further gate.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Empties then auto-refills on use; the player is immune to damage during the refill animation, though PvP-world attackers still gain xp on a landed hit.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Free to replace from Velorina in Port Phasmatys (needs a ghostspeak amulet or better) or bought from Perdu for a flat fee if lost.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Like other teleports in this KB it stops working above level 20 Wilderness.

summary: Book of the dead is required to cast Necromancy resurrection spells, awarded via A Kingdom Divided with Kharedst's memoirs teleports plus more charges.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Equipable book required to cast resurrection spells (Necromancy); awarded on completing A Kingdom Divided.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: A Kingdom Divided is a hard prerequisite for casting any resurrection spell, since the book is the item-form gate for that spell family.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Carries the same teleport destinations as Kharedst's memoirs (the five Kourend House teleports) with 150 extra charge capacity (250 max once all 5 Kharedst pages are collected, vs. the memoirs' 100).

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Free to reclaim from Commander Fullore in Kourend Castle if lost; an extra copy can be bought from Perdu for 9,500 coins.

req_items.note: buys an extra copy from Perdu, optional

summary: Rada's blessing (tiers 1-4) is an ammo-slot item from Elise per Kourend & Kebos Diary tier; the elite tier gives the best ammo-slot Prayer bonus plus teleports.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Ammo-slot item awarded by Elise in the Kourend Castle courtyard for each Kourend & Kebos Diary tier; free to reclaim if lost.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The gate is Kourend & Kebos Diary tier completion rather than a craftable-item recipe.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Elite tier (blessing 4) gives the best-in-slot ammo-slot Prayer bonus (+2, beats god blessings), unlimited teleports to both Kourend Woodland and Mount Karuulm, and an 8% chance per catch to land an extra fish everywhere (no bonus xp/bait).

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Lower tiers grant a subset: smaller Prayer bonus, fewer/no teleport destinations, lower fish-bonus chance.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Stackable in the ammo slot alongside main-hand/off-hand gear, so it does not conflict with weapon choice.

summary: Barrows gloves are strong all-combat-style gloves bought for 130,000 coins after finishing the entire Recipe for Disaster quest chain.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Second-highest Melee offensive bonuses (behind ferocious gloves), second-highest Ranged offensive bonuses (behind zaryte vambraces), third-highest Magic offensive bonuses (behind tormented bracelet/confliction gauntlets), with no Defence requirement to equip.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: Requires completing the entire Recipe for Disaster quest chain (10 subquest chapters plus the master quest), one of the largest single requisite bundles in the game.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: In practice needs roughly Defence 35, accumulated from RFD's own quest/xp requirements rather than a stated explicit Defence requirement on the gloves.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Bought for 130,000 coins from the Culinaromancer's Chest in the Lumbridge Castle cellar (104,000 after the Elite Lumbridge & Draynor Diary).

facts.label: hazard
facts.value: In PvP death without protection they revert to 78,000 coins instead of dropping the item itself.

summary: Fire cape is the second-best melee cape, earned by killing TzTok-Jad at the end of the TzHaar Fight Cave; it is also the entry item for the Inferno.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Second-best melee cape in the game (behind only the infernal cape), earned by completing a run of the TzHaar Fight Cave ending in a kill on TzTok-Jad.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Award requires the game to recognise Jad's death, not the player's own death; even simultaneous deaths do not award the cape.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: Sacrificed to TzHaar-Ket-Keh as the one-time entry fee to unlock the Inferno, gateway to the infernal cape.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Functions as the access key to deeper Mor Ul Rek, shown to TzHaar-Ket guards, not consumed by that use.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: No formal skill/quest/item prerequisite exists for entry -- the gate is purely a combat-performance check (survive every Fight Cave wave then kill Jad).

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: If lost unprotected in PvP it becomes a repairable broken cape (Perdu, 150,000 coins) rather than being destroyed outright.

summary: Void Knight equipment needs 42 in every combat skill plus 22 Prayer and is bought with Pest Control commendation points; a full basic set costs 850 minimum.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Full armour set giving equal Defence bonuses across every combat style (Melee/Ranged/Magic) without lowering attack bonuses, plus a set-effect combat-style damage/accuracy bonus when a full matching set (helm+top+robe+gloves, style-matched) is worn.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Entry gate is a flat stat check: 42 Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints, Ranged, and Magic, plus 22 Prayer -- no quest requirement.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Bought with Pest Control commendation points: 850 minimum for one full basic set including one helm (excluding mace/seal); +400 for the elite top+robe (1,250 total); +400 more for the other two helms (1,650 total for a complete elite set in every combat style).

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Upgradeable per-piece to Elite Void (top/robe only) with additional commendation points once the Hard Western Provinces Diary is done.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: The commendation-point-farming activity itself is documented separately under minigamedb:pest-control; this row covers only the purchase-side stat/point costs and set-effect payoff.

summary: Shades of Mort'ton is a repeatable multi-skill minigame from its own quest, cremating shade remains for Firemaking/Prayer xp, keys, coins, oil, catacomb loot.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Repeatable minigame unlocked by completing the Shades of Mort'ton quest, which teaches the core loop: brew Serum 207/208 from Herblore, repair the temple with Crafting, cremate shade remains into keys/coins/xp with Firemaking+Prayer.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: A Serum 208 dose used on Razmire Keelgan during or after the quest grants permanent shop access.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Repeat play runs on a personal Sanctity resource (0-100%, decays 1%/min, resets to 0 on logout), raised by spending building resources on temple repair (~5% Sanctity per 1% resources spent) or by killing nearby shades (2% per kill).

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Sanctity unlocks sanctifying olive oil into sacred oil (10%+ Sanctity, 0.9% cost per dose) or brewing Serum 208 at the temple's fire altar (20%+ Sanctity, 5% cost per dose).

facts.label: hazard
facts.value: Loar shades (level 40, no key needed) wander Mort'ton freely and can aggro/chase from long range in this single-way combat zone.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: The five higher shade tiers (Phrin/Riyl/Asyn/Fiyr/Urium, level 60-140) live behind keyed doors in the Shade Catacombs, requiring progressively rarer bronze-to-gold keys obtained only by cremating shade remains of the matching or adjacent tier -- each cremation is a probabilistic key-or-coins roll, roughly 21% coins otherwise a key.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Repairing the temple with a Flamtaer hammer gives roughly 12 Crafting xp/second, one of the cheapest Crafting-xp methods by material cost though slow.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Chest loot scales by key tier: Bronze (Steel-Mithril items + easy clues), Steel (Steel-Adamant + medium clues), Black (Black-Adamant + medium clues), Silver (Black-Rune + hard clues), Gold (Adamant-Dragon + elite clues, plus Zealot's robes).

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Coffin locks (bronze-gold) traded to Dampe outside the catacombs upgrade a broken coffin into an equippable cape-slot shade-remains container, holding 3 (bronze) up to 28 (gold); Runescroll of swampbark and Runescroll of bloodbark unlock crafting swampbark/bloodbark armour from splitbark armour.

summary: Rat Pits is a 2-player PvP cat-fighting gambling minigame across 4 city pits, staking 100-20,000 coins with no xp reward; ironmen cannot play.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: 2-player-only PvP gambling minigame across four separate underground pits (Ardougne, Varrock, Keldagrim, Port Sarim), each accepting only one specific cat growth stage.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: Ironmen are hard-locked out entirely.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: Each pit unlocks individually as the player helps that pit's owner during the Ratcatchers quest, not an all-or-nothing gate.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: A catspeak amulet (or Dragon Slayer II's innate catspeak) lets the owner pick one of 4 tactical dialogue options trading Attack/Strength for Defence/Hitpoints and whether the cat flees at low health vs fights to the death; without any strategy control the cat fights to the death by default.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Winner takes the matched coin bet (100-20,000gp) from the loser; a draw (both cats tire out at equal rat-kills) returns both bets untouched.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Ardougne and Varrock pit wins additionally advance the cat's growth timer by roughly 15 minutes on a win, 7.5 minutes on a loss.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: No xp reward for playing.

req_items.name: cat (growth stage matching the pit)
req_items.note: kitten for Ardougne, cat for Varrock, overgrown cat for Keldagrim, wily cat for Port Sarim; lazy cats are banned everywhere and must be trained up to wily via Felkrash at the Port Sarim pit first

req_items.name: catspeak amulet
req_items.note: not needed if Dragon Slayer II is completed, which grants catspeak innately; without strategy control the cat fights to the death by default

req_items.note: 100-20,000 to bet; both players must match stakes

summary: Gnome Ball is a free-for-all Agility/Ranged sports minigame at the Tree Gnome Stronghold pitch, first to 5 goals, with no entry requirement.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Free-for-all sports minigame with no entry requirement; weapons are auto-unequipped into inventory on entry.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Players Pass (to teammates or the two green gnome wingers), Tackle (success scaled by Agility; being tackled while holding the ball transfers it to the tackler plus 1-2 damage), or Shoot (success scaled by Ranged level and proximity to goal) to score; first to 5 points wins and their score resets.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: 4-7 xp per goal scored in both Agility and Ranged, plus a flat 25 xp bonus in each skill for winning.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: One tradeable, GE-priced gnomeball is awarded on winning a game, capped at one per game; players who brought their own gnomeball onto the pitch don't get a second one from winning.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: Scoring one goal is an Easy Western Provinces Diary requirement.

facts.label: hazard
facts.value: Being tackled deals 1-2 chip damage, a consideration for players with low Hitpoints.

summary: Impetuous Impulses is the concentrated impling-catching minigame at Puro-Puro, Hunter-gated per impling tier, reached via the Zanaris crop circle.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: A maze of magical wheat rows at Puro-Puro (pushable through with high Strength) where implings of many tiers spawn and must be caught, functionally the concentrated version of impling hunting otherwise done across the overworld.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Hunter 17 minimum to enter the maze and catch the lowest tier (baby impling) with a net and jar; 27 to catch it barehanded without a net (the barehanded threshold is +10 over the netted minimum for every tier), though a jar is still needed to carry a barehanded catch out.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: Lost City is needed only for the permanent Zanaris crop-circle portal shortcut -- no quest is required to reach Puro-Puro via the migratory surface crop circles found by talking to the wandering impling in Zanaris' wheat field.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Elnock Inquisitor at the entrance gives a free butterfly net, 7 starter impling jars, and an impling scroll that tracks catches per type on first entry.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Elnock's Exchange barter shop converts caught jars into catching aids: 3 baby+2 young+1 gourmet jars -> Imp repellent; 3 gourmet+2 earth+1 essence jars -> Magic butterfly net; 3 essence+2 eclectic+1 nature jars -> Jar generator; 1 jar of any type -> 3 empty impling jars.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Nearly every impling type in the game (baby through lucky) spawns here; the sole exception is the crystal impling, which is Prifddinas-only.

facts.label: caveat
facts.value: A daily gold-coin jar purchase cap of 10 applies at Elnock's Exchange.

summary: Sorceress's Garden is a stealth Thieving/Farming/Cooking minigame in four seasonal instanced gardens near Al Kharid, Thieving-gated 25/45/65 by season.

facts.label: overview
facts.value: Sneak past guardian elementals in one of four seasonal instanced gardens to steal either one sq'irk fruit or 2 random herbs per entry, then get auto-teleported back to the central fountain-garden hub.

facts.label: mechanics
facts.value: Thieving 25 for Spring, 45 for Autumn, 65 for Summer gates each seasonal garden's sq'irk tree and herb patch (Winter needs none); boosts, including from the sq'irkjuice reward itself, count toward the gate.

facts.label: hazard
facts.value: Getting spotted by an elemental, which can only detect/teleport the player within 2 tiles, ejects the player empty-handed.

facts.label: required-for
facts.value: Started via Prince Ali Rescue (talk to Osman); Beneath Cursed Sands additionally unlocks Selim as an alternate quest-giver for the same minigame.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Herb picks give a flat 50 Farming xp (25 xp/herb, always 2 clean herbs) independent of season; crushing a sq'irk into juice gives a flat 5 Cooking xp independent of season.

facts.label: xp-note
facts.value: Turning sq'irkjuice in to Osman/Selim gives 350 (Winter) / 1,350 (Spring) / 2,350 (Autumn) / 3,000 (Summer) Thieving xp per juice.

facts.label: items-note
facts.value: Random clean herbs per garden tier: Winter (guam/marrentill/tarromin/harralander only), Spring adds irit+avantoe, Autumn adds ranarr+kwuarm+cadantine, Summer adds lantadyme+dwarf weed -- higher seasons strictly superset lower ones.

facts.label: unlock
facts.value: Sq'irkjuice can alternatively be drunk instead of turned in, for a temporary Thieving boost (0/+1/+2/+3 by season) plus a run-energy restore (5%/10%/15%/20% by season).
